sentences.text: A defining feature of this dinosaur is a tall, curved crest made of nasal and prefrontal bones that resembles a scimitar and stands half a meter high.
The holotype, representing a subadult, is estimated to reach a total length of 8 meters.
Scientists hypothesize that a fully mature individual could have grown to between 10 and 14 meters long.
Remains were gathered in Niger at sites named Iguidi and Jenguebi during digs between 2000 and 2022 led by Paul Sereno.
This species was officially named in a study published in Science on February 19, 2026, by Sereno and his team.
Evidence from interior river sediments suggests it was a wading hunter that ambushed prey in shallow water.
It is considered a close relative of the sail-backed, fish-eating giant Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.
Taxonomically, it is a spinosaurid theropod belonging to the subfamily Spinosaurinae, and phylogenetic analysis places it as the sister group to Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.
It lived 95 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) within the Farak Formation, a river system made of sandstone and sandy shale.
Some fossils once assigned to Carcharodontosaurus may actually belong to a spinosaurid, as certain neck vertebrae were incorrectly linked to C. saharicus.
Views on its lifestyle vary, oscillating between a semi-aquatic ambush predator and a fully aquatic animal with active diving skills.
Researchers also propose that the evolution of spinosaurids happened in three separate phases.
